title: Additive representations by powerful integers
summary: A saving of 1/(153k) for primitive diagonal powerful triples using minimum-energy subsets, adaptive amplification and a choice of fixed summand.
abstract:
For all sufficiently large \(k\), the number of primitive
\(k\)-full triples \(a+b=c\le X\) is
\(O_{k,\varepsilon}(X^{(2-1/153)/k+\varepsilon})\).
We compress each triple at fixed \(c\) to a rational congruence
and count its solutions using a rectangular determinant.
A minimum-energy subset controls the loss of precision
under Newton divided differences. The partition depth and
amplification order depend on the factorization of the modulus. For fixed offsets \(p=r+u,\ q=r+v\)
we also save a fixed multiple of \(1/r\) over \(1/p+1/q\).
For representations by two positive \(k\)-full integers,
we give pointwise bounds of \(O_\varepsilon(N^{3/10+\varepsilon})\) for \(k=2\)
and \(O_{k,\varepsilon}(N^{1/(k+1)+\varepsilon})\) for \(k\ge3\).
The graph bounds for these estimates apply also to large
coprime differences.
